    OIDC¶

    Requires the oidc extra:

    uv add "rn-forge-auth[oidc]"

    rn_forge.auth.oidc is not re-exported from rn_forge.auth — import it directly:

    from rn_forge.auth.oidc import OidcAuthenticator

    rn_forge.auth.oidc ¶

    OIDC: discovery, the login provider, one validation profile per kind of token (access, ID and logout) and the authenticator that maps verified access-token claims to a :class:~rn_forge.auth.Principal.

    :class:OidcProvider runs the authorization code flow with PKCE over Authlib's OAuth2Session and verifies the ID token with :class:IdTokenVerifier.

    A token is accepted only by the profile used at its own place: the claims and the typ header each profile requires exclude the others.

    :class:TokenVerificationError carries the specific failure reason. Log it; never send it to the client.

    Requires the oidc extra. Not imported by :mod:rn_forge.auth; import this module directly.

    ClaimMapper = Callable[[str, Mapping[str, Any]], ExternalIdentity] ¶

    Maps (provider ID, verified claims) to an identity.

    The claims are the ID token's, completed by UserInfo for any claim the ID token lacks. Raise :class:~rn_forge.auth.LoginFailed to refuse the login.

    BackchannelLogout(verifier, accounts) ¶

    Validates a back-channel logout token and says what it revokes.

    The handler changes no state besides the verifier's jti record: the binding applies the returned :class:LogoutRevocation, because the revoked-sid lifetime (the sessions' absolute timeout) and the session-version store belong to it.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    verifier LogoutTokenVerifier

    The logout-token profile for this provider.

    		 required
    accounts AccountResolver

    Finds the account behind (issuer, sub); never provisions.

    		 required

    handle(logout_token) ¶

    Verify logout_token and return what to revoke.

    A token with a sid revokes that session only, even if it also has a sub.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TokenVerificationError

    The token fails the logout-token profile, including a replayed jti. The message is for logs; answer 400.

    JwtVerifier(*, jwks, issuer, audience, algorithms=('RS256',), leeway=0.0, mode='rfc7519', login_client_id=None) ¶

    The access-token profile: verify a bearer JWT against a key set, an issuer and an audience.

    mode="rfc9068" accepts only RFC 9068 access tokens: a typ header of at+jwt or application/at+jwt (case-insensitive), and iss, exp, aud, sub, client_id, iat and jti present. mode="rfc7519" accepts a typ of JWT (case-insensitive) or none, requires iss, aud and exp, and validates sub, nbf and iat when present.

    In both modes a token carrying nonce or events (an ID token or a logout token) is rejected, iss must equal the configured issuer, and aud must contain one of the configured audiences. The algorithm allow-list is what rejects alg: none and an HMAC token signed with the public key.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    jwks PyJWKClient

    Where signing keys come from. It caches the key set and refetches for an unknown kid at most once per its cooldown_duration.

    		 required
    issuer str

    The exact iss accepted.

    		 required
    audience str | Sequence[str]

    The aud accepted — one value, or any of several.

    		 required
    algorithms Sequence[str]

    The signature algorithms accepted.

    		 ('RS256',)
    leeway float

    Seconds of clock skew tolerated on exp/nbf/iat.

    		 0.0
    mode TokenMode

    The access-token standard the provider issues.

    		 'rfc7519'
    login_client_id str | None

    The OIDC login client ID of this application, if any.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    login_client_id is one of the accepted audiences and mode is not "rfc9068".

    LogoutRevocation(issuer, sid=None, subject=None, account_id=None) dataclass ¶

    What a valid back-channel logout token asks to revoke.

    With a sid, revoke that one session: ReplayStore.revoke_sid(issuer, sid, ...). Without one, bump the session version of account_id, or do nothing when it is None.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    issuer str

    The token's iss.
    sid str | None

    The session ID to revoke, if the token names one.
    subject str | None

    The token's sub, if present.
    account_id str | None

    For a token without sid, the account linked to (issuer, subject); None when none is linked.

    LogoutTokenVerifier(*, jwks, issuer, client_id, replay_store, algorithms=('RS256',), leeway=0.0, max_age_seconds=120.0) ¶

    The logout-token profile: verify an OIDC Back-Channel Logout token.

    Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.6 requires iss, aud, iat, exp, jti and events; events must be an object whose http://schemas.openid.net/event/backchannel-logout member is an object; sid or sub must be present; nonce must be absent. Added here: the typ header is logout+jwt (optionally prefixed application/, case-insensitive) or absent; iat is at most max_age_seconds old; and a jti is accepted once. The jti is recorded in replay_store under "{iss}|{jti}" until the token's exp (at least one second), after every other check has passed.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    jwks PyJWKClient

    Where signing keys come from.

    		 required
    issuer str

    The exact iss accepted.

    		 required
    client_id str

    The OIDC login client ID; the aud expected.

    		 required
    replay_store ReplayStore

    Remembers the jti values already accepted.

    		 required
    algorithms Sequence[str]

    The signature algorithms accepted.

    		 ('RS256',)
    leeway float

    Seconds of clock skew tolerated.

    		 0.0
    max_age_seconds float

    The oldest iat, in seconds, accepted.

    		 120.0

    OidcAuthenticator(verifier, *, claims_to_principal=principal_from_claims) ¶

    An :class:~rn_forge.auth.Authenticator backed by a :class:JwtVerifier.

    The verifier holds the JWKS cache; build one authenticator and reuse it.

    The reason a token was rejected is carried on the raised :class:~rn_forge.web.exceptions.AuthenticationFailed, for logging. It is not part of the 401 response body, which is :data:~rn_forge.web.AUTH_FAILED_DETAIL.

    Parameters:

    		 required

    Verified claims → principal. Defaults to :func:~rn_forge.auth.principal_from_claims.

    		 principal_from_claims

    OidcProvider(*, id, issuer, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, scopes=None, max_age=None, userinfo='auto', claim_mapper=default_claim_mapper, token_hook=None, fetch=fetch_json, algorithms=('RS256',), leeway=0.0, timeout=5.0, token_endpoint_auth_method='client_secret_basic', rp_initiated_logout=False, endpoints=None, subject_field='sub', response_issuer=None) ¶

    Bases: IdentityProvider[LoginRequest]

    An OIDC :class:~rn_forge.auth.IdentityProvider: authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), over Authlib's OAuth2Session.

    The authorization request carries state, a nonce, the PKCE challenge and max_age when set; all of them are recorded on the login transaction. The callback is accepted only when its state equals the transaction's, its iss (RFC 9207) names the issuer, the code exchange succeeds and the ID token satisfies :class:IdTokenVerifier. The upstream tokens are discarded unless token_hook is given.

    :meth:oauth2 builds the provider for a server with no ID token: kind is "oauth2", the request carries no nonce, and the identity comes from the user endpoint called with the access token.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    id str

    The provider ID.

    		 required
    issuer str

    The IdP's issuer URL; its discovery document is read on first use. For an OAuth 2.0 provider, the fixed issuer of its identities.

    		 required
    client_id str

    The registered client.

    		 required
    client_secret str | None

    The client's secret; None for a public client.

    		 required
    redirect_uri str

    The registered callback URL.

    		 required
    scopes Sequence[str] | None

    The requested scopes; OIDC requires openid. Defaults to openid email profile, or to none for an OAuth 2.0 provider.

    		 None
    max_age int | None

    When set, the most seconds since the user authenticated; sent on the authorization request and enforced on the ID token.

    		 None
    userinfo UserInfoMode

    "always" calls the UserInfo endpoint, "never" does not, and "auto" calls it when the ID token has no email. The UserInfo sub must equal the ID token's.

    		 'auto'
    claim_mapper ClaimMapper

    Replaces :func:default_claim_mapper.

    		 default_claim_mapper
    token_hook TokenHook | None

    Called with the identity and the upstream tokens after a successful login.

    		 None
    fetch FetchJson

    The transport for the discovery document.

    		 fetch_json
    algorithms Sequence[str]

    The ID-token signature algorithms accepted.

    		 ('RS256',)
    leeway float

    Seconds of clock skew tolerated.

    		 0.0
    timeout float

    Seconds before a back-channel request fails.

    		 5.0
    token_endpoint_auth_method str

    How the client authenticates at the token endpoint.

    		 'client_secret_basic'
    rp_initiated_logout bool

    Whether :meth:logout_redirect returns the provider's end_session_endpoint. Ignored for an OAuth 2.0 provider, which has none.

    		 False
    endpoints OAuth2Endpoints | None

    When given, makes an OAuth 2.0 provider; see :meth:oauth2.

    		 None
    subject_field str

    The user-endpoint member that is the subject.

    		 'sub'
    response_issuer str | None

    The iss an OAuth 2.0 authorization response must carry; None skips the check.

    		 None

    Name Type Description
    id

    The provider ID.
    kind ProviderKind

    "oidc", or "oauth2" for an OAuth 2.0 provider.

    str | None

    oauth2(*, id, issuer, endpoints, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, scopes=(), subject_field='sub', response_issuer=None, claim_mapper=default_claim_mapper, token_hook=None, timeout=5.0, token_endpoint_auth_method='client_secret_basic') classmethod ¶

    Build a provider for an OAuth 2.0 server that issues no ID token.

    The flow keeps state and PKCE and sends no nonce. After the code exchange the user endpoint is called with the access token; its JSON object is the claim set, with iss set to issuer and sub set to the subject_field member as a string (numbers are stringified), then passed to claim_mapper.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    id str

    The provider ID.

    		 required
    issuer str

    The fixed issuer of the identities.

    		 required
    endpoints OAuth2Endpoints

    The provider's endpoints.

    		 required
    client_id str

    The registered client.

    		 required
    client_secret str | None

    The client's secret; None for a public client.

    		 required
    redirect_uri str

    The registered callback URL.

    		 required
    scopes Sequence[str]

    The requested scopes.

    		 ()
    subject_field str

    The user-endpoint member that is the subject, such as "id".

    		 'sub'
    response_issuer str | None

    The iss the authorization response must carry; None skips the check, as for a provider that sends none.

    		 None
    claim_mapper ClaimMapper

    Replaces :func:default_claim_mapper.

    		 default_claim_mapper
    token_hook TokenHook | None

    Called with the identity and the upstream tokens.

    		 None
    timeout float

    Seconds before a back-channel request fails.

    		 5.0
    token_endpoint_auth_method str

    How the client authenticates at the token endpoint.

    		 'client_secret_basic'

    TokenVerificationError(message, *message_args, error_code=-1, **error_data) ¶

    Bases: AppException

    A token, a key set or a discovery document failed verification.

    The message says why. It is for logs: a 401 body must not repeat it.

    default_claim_mapper(provider, claims) ¶

    Map standard OIDC claims to an :class:~rn_forge.auth.ExternalIdentity.

    sub, email, email_verified, name, picture, groups, auth_time and amr fill the fields of the same name, and sid fills session_ref. A claim of the wrong type is ignored. Every other claim except the token-protocol ones (iss, aud, exp, iat, nbf, jti, nonce, at_hash, c_hash, azp) goes to attributes.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    LoginFailed

    sub or iss is missing.

    discover_oidc(issuer, *, fetch=fetch_json) ¶

    Read issuer's /.well-known/openid-configuration.

    Per RFC 8414 §3.3, the document's issuer must equal the issuer it was fetched for; a mismatch is an error.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TokenVerificationError

    The document is unreachable, lacks issuer or jwks_uri, or names a different issuer.
